title: Intelligent Monitoring and Warning for Road‐Network Tunnels Via Feature Matching
content:
To address the safety issues in mountain tunnel construction, an early warning model integrating association rules and text vectorization feature matching was developed. The validation on two tunnels demonstrated that this model can accurately predict accident types and actively identify risks, providing support for dynamic safety management and the formulation of targeted prevention and control measures.


ABSTRACT

Mountain tunnel construction involves complex geological conditions and frequent cross-operations, making safety accident prevention particularly challenging. To enhance the foresight and specificity of construction safety management, this paper develops a feature element system for safety accidents in mountain tunnel construction from the “object–cause–consequence” three-dimensional perspective, and establishes a safety accident early warning model that integrates association rule mining and text vectorization techniques. First, based on 145 real-world mountain tunnel construction safety accident cases, the TF-IDF algorithm and k-means clustering are used to extract and condense 6 types of object elements, 5 categories (20 specific items) of cause elements, and 10 types of consequence elements. Second, the Apriori algorithm is applied to mine strong association rules among “object–cause–consequence” triplets, resulting in a corpus of 41 accident rule chains. The Word2vec word embedding model and Pearson similarity calculation are then combined to match target cases against these rule chains. Finally, a simple majority principle and a fluctuation principle are introduced to define warning thresholds, establishing a three-tier early warning mechanism. Two empirical studies are carried out: one on the XCS tunnel, where an accident actually occurred, and the other on the DPS3 tunnel of the GN railway, which has not experienced accidents. The results indicate that the XCS tunnel triggered a red warning in the excavation zone, predicting a possible collapse or roof fall accident, which aligns well with the actual collapse that happened. The DPS3 tunnel, in its support and lining zone, also triggered a red warning, signaling the risk of collapse and roof fall. These findings provide methodological support for dynamic safety control and precise early warning in mountain tunnel construction.
